section_summary: This section opens with correspondence between the American Committee for Non-Participation in Japanese Aggression and the State Department concerning the booklet “America’s Share in Japan’s War Guilt.” Most of the section consists of the booklet itself, which argues that American exports of oil, metals, machinery, aircraft, and other strategic goods sustained Japan’s invasion of China and advocates embargoes, boycotts, labor action, and revised neutrality legislation. It assembles trade statistics and statements from government officials, members of Congress, journalists, clergy, labor leaders, Chinese and Japanese officials, and civic organizations.

subfiles.title: Letter transmitting “America’s Share in Japan’s War Guilt”
subfiles.from: Harry B. Price, Secretary, American Committee for Non-Participation in Japanese Aggression
subfiles.to: Sumner Welles, Under Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Transmits a complimentary copy of the committee’s booklet on American economic participation in Japan’s war in China.
subfiles.summary: Price tells Welles that a copy of “America’s Share in Japan’s War Guilt” is being sent under separate cover. He describes the subject as one of the most important foreign-policy issues confronting Americans and asks for Welles’s careful consideration. The committee’s national board and initial members are listed in the letterhead.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of receipt of “America’s Share in Japan’s War Guilt”
subfiles.from: Maxwell M. Hamilton, Chief, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.to: Harry B. Price, Secretary, American Committee for Non-Participation in Japanese Aggression
subfiles.about: Acknowledges copies of the committee’s booklet sent to State Department officials.
subfiles.summary: Hamilton acknowledges Price’s August 24 letters to the Secretary of State and Sumner Welles and confirms receipt of the booklet. He expresses appreciation for copies supplied to those officials and to other Department officers, including himself.

subfiles.title: America’s Share in Japan’s War Guilt
subfiles.from: American Committee for Non-Participation in Japanese Aggression
subfiles.about: Argues that American trade sustains Japanese aggression in China and urges an end to exports, financing, and other economic assistance useful to Japan’s war effort.
subfiles.summary: The pamphlet’s foreword characterizes American sales of oil, metals, aircraft, machinery, and vehicles as material participation in Japan’s invasion of China and calls for a policy of non-cooperation. It supports its case with import statistics, discussion of the Neutrality Act and treaty obligations, and a lengthy question-and-answer defense of embargoes and economic pressure. Statements from executive officials, senators, representatives, journalists, clergy, labor leaders, Chiang Kai-shek, Japanese officials, and civic organizations condemn civilian bombing or debate how American policy should respond. The closing pages in this section reproduce resolutions favoring embargoes, boycotts, revised neutrality legislation, and coordinated moral and economic action against aggressor states.
